speaker: narrator
text: Act IV: The Final Confrontation

speaker: narrator
text: With the lifelight elixir in your pack, you stand before Malakar's fortress. Mira steps through the gates beside you, her hands still unsteady from the circle. She and Sir Cedric stop just inside the threshold. A small light settles on the gatepost: Nyx, keeping close.

speaker: mira
text: I said I would come with you, and I have. Someone has to keep the way out open, and that's me. So come back through it.

speaker: sir cedric
text: I held a gate once and lost a king behind it. I will not lose this one, or you.

speaker: nyx
text: I'll be the light at the edge of your eye. Don't look for me. Just know.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira presses something into your hand: a small silver medallion, two hands clasped on its face. Sir Cedric lays his hand over hers; the light on the gatepost leans in.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive a loyalty token.

speaker: mira
text: If it goes quiet in there, say our names. We'll hear.

speaker: narrator
text: The rest of the way is yours to walk, but they will not be far.

speaker: narrator
text: Fortress Gates

speaker: narrator
text: You stand just inside the fortress gates. The ways on, north and east, are barred by a thin wall of violet light, and three ward stones, left, middle and right, swell and fade with it. Guardians made of shadow drift between the stones, watching you. On the arch behind you, under the black, an older carving shows through: a sun rising over three linked rings. Just inside the threshold Mira keeps the way out, her back to the gatepost.

speaker: narrator
text: The left stone swells and fades with the barrier, exactly on the beat.

speaker: narrator
text: The middle stone swells and fades with the barrier, exactly on the beat.

speaker: narrator
text: The right stone brightens a breath after the barrier does, every time, like a man who has lost count.

speaker: narrator
text: Three ward stones stand inside the gates, evenly spaced, each carved with the same runes. Their light swells and fades together, and the barrier swells and fades with them. All but one: the right stone brightens a breath after the others, like a man who has lost count.

speaker: narrator
text: A thin wall of violet light hangs across the ways on, north and east, humming in time with the ward stones. It is the only thing between you and the fortress.

speaker: narrator
text: A family heirloom whose runes glint like dew at dawn. In its depths Aren and Lysa stand hand in hand. The third figure keeps his back turned.

speaker: narrator
text: A shimmering elixir that seems to contain liquid starlight. Threads of crystal clarity, phoenix flame, and draconic essence swirl within the glass vial.

speaker: narrator
text: A small silver medallion stamped with two clasped hands, warm from the friends who pressed it into your hand. Whoever carries it is not alone, and knows it.

speaker: narrator
text: A small crystalline pendant that shifts through the colours of the forest as you turn it: leaf green, acorn brown, snow, blossom. It is warm, the way a held hand is warm.

speaker: narrator
text: A crystal with a whole small forest in it. Tiny lights move inside like fireflies, and held close it sounds faintly of wind in leaves.

speaker: narrator
text: The token is warm in your hand. Someone, somewhere, is glad you came.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Fortress Gates, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: You think it over. Nothing presses on you just now.

speaker: narrator
text: You rest for a moment, gathering your strength.

speaker: narrator
text: New main quest

speaker: narrator
text: The Final Stand

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar's fortress. Somewhere inside it King Alden is held, and Malakar waits for you. You came to free the king, and to make Malakar pay for what he took.

speaker: narrator
text: New side quest

speaker: narrator
text: Shattered Ward Guardians

speaker: narrator
text: Shadow guardians and a wall of violet light bar the way into the fortress. Find what feeds them, and break their hold on the gates.

speaker: narrator
text: The violet wall throws you back. It swells and fades in time with the ward stones.

speaker: narrator
text: Your light falls on the guardians and slides off them. They stand on the barrier, and the barrier stands on the stones.

speaker: narrator
text: The stone drinks your light and pulses brighter, and the guardians lean closer for a moment. The barrier keeps its rhythm.

speaker: narrator
text: Your light washes over all three stones at once. They drink it together and keep their count.

speaker: narrator
text: You channel divine energy, filling the area with warm, golden light, but there is nothing here that responds to the blessing.

speaker: narrator
text: You stop and think over what you know.

speaker: narrator
text: The Final Stand: Malakar's fortress. Somewhere inside it King Alden is held, and Malakar waits for you. You came to free the king, and to make Malakar pay for what he took.

speaker: narrator
text: Shattered Ward Guardians: Shadow guardians and a wall of violet light bar the way into the fortress. Find what feeds them, and break their hold on the gates.

speaker: narrator
text: Your light finds the right stone between its beats. It flares, stutters, and goes dark. A fragment cracks from its face and drops to the flagstones. The other two stones falter, lose the count, and go dark with it; the barrier flickers out of time and is gone.

speaker: narrator
text: Without the barrier the guardians have nothing to stand on. They thin to smoke, and where they drifted lie the guardian's chain that bound them and a small, steady light: the guardian's essence.

speaker: narrator
text: Side quest complete

speaker: narrator
text: Elior's light breaks the guardians' hold on the gates. The ward stones fall dark, and the way into Malakar's fortress lies open.

speaker: narrator
text: The stone is dark. Your light shows only its runes.

speaker: narrator
text: The ward stones are dark. Your light shows only their runes.

speaker: narrator
text: The fragment is lighter than it looks, and cold.

speaker: narrator
text: The left stone is dark.

speaker: narrator
text: The middle stone is dark.

speaker: narrator
text: The right stone is dark.

speaker: narrator
text: Three ward stones, dark and silent. The right one is missing a piece of its face.

speaker: narrator
text: The violet wall is gone. The way on is only a way now.

speaker: narrator
text: A jagged piece of the right ward stone, carved with half a rune. It is cold, and keeps no time at all.

speaker: narrator
text: A silver chain set with small crystals, each link inscribed with runes. It bound the guardians to the stones; now it binds nothing.

speaker: narrator
text: A small, steady light the colour of a candle flame, left where the last guardian stood. Whoever the guardians were made from was brave once. The light remembers it.

speaker: narrator
text: The chain is warm, and its crystals brighten a little in your hands.

speaker: narrator
text: The light shows it clearly, but has no special effect.

speaker: narrator
text: The crystals stay quiet. Whatever the chain was made to stand against, it is not here.

speaker: narrator
text: This might come in handy, so you decide to pick it up.

speaker: narrator
text: The light sits warm in your hand, waiting for someone to show it to.

speaker: narrator
text: The Trapped Servants

speaker: narrator
text: The king's servants walk the courtyard in chains of shadow. Win their trust, and break the chains.

speaker: narrator
text: The servants flinch from the light and keep walking. They do not know you, and they have learned what strangers bring.

speaker: narrator
text: The room is already well lit.

speaker: narrator
text: The servants drift across the archway, their chains trailing. They do not stop for you, and you cannot get past them.

speaker: narrator
text: Captain of the Guard glows briefly with golden light.

speaker: narrator
text: The captain stares through you. His hands do not close on it, and you keep it.

speaker: narrator
text: Outer Courtyard

speaker: narrator
text: This was a garden once. The fountains still stand under a sky that never quite rains, but what runs down them is black and slow, and the statues have all turned their faces away. Grey figures walk the paths in circles, chains of shadow at their ankles, never looking up. By the dry fountain a soldier in a soot-black royal tabard stands rigid, staring at nothing.

speaker: narrator
text: The light warms your hands. Across the courtyard, one of the servants stops walking and turns towards it.

speaker: narrator
text: The Trapped Servants watch you from the corners of their eyes and keep walking. One whispers, without stopping:

speaker: trapped servants
text: Others came through that gate. They were all brave, until the guardians. If you were braver than the guardians, you would carry something of theirs.

speaker: narrator
text: The Captain of the Guard stares through you.

speaker: captain of the guard
text: I kept King Alden's gate once. Now I keep it for... I cannot remember.

speaker: narrator
text: Grey figures walk the courtyard paths in circles, chains of shadow at their ankles. They wear what is left of kitchen aprons and stable coats. None of them looks up.

speaker: narrator
text: A captain of the royal guard, his tabard black with soot. His eyes are open but see nothing, and his hand rests on a sword he has forgotten how to draw.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Outer Courtyard, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The Trapped Servants: The king's servants walk the courtyard in chains of shadow. Win their trust, and break the chains.

speaker: narrator
text: The servants stop their circling and gather to look at the guardian's essence. One reaches out, but does not touch. They know what it is, and what it cost. For the first time, they look at you instead of through you.

speaker: narrator
text: The Trapped Servants have stopped walking. They stand close together, watching you.

speaker: trapped servants
text: We are so tired. No one has said a kind word over us since we came here. Whatever you can do for us, do it gently.

speaker: narrator
text: Your blessing settles over the courtyard like warm light through a window. The chains do not break so much as forget to hold, and fall away. One by one the servants stand still and look up. By the fountain, the captain blinks, as if waking from a long sleep. One of the servants lays a small blue servant's pendant on the fountain's rim for you.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior's courage earns the servants' trust, and a blessing breaks their chains. Freed, they leave him a pendant to light the way.

speaker: narrator
text: You lift the guardian's chain over the captain's head. Its crystals flare once and settle against his soot-black tabard, and the warmth goes out of your hands.

speaker: narrator
text: The Captain of the Guard puts a hand to the chain.

speaker: captain of the guard
text: You will need this more than I will.

speaker: narrator
text: He tries to give it back, and when you will not take it, he grips your arm.

speaker: captain of the guard
text: Then I will tell them at home what you did here.

speaker: narrator
text: He turns toward the gates. The shadows draw away from the light at his throat, and at the arch he lifts a hand to you before he goes.

speaker: narrator
text: The Maze of Mirrors

speaker: narrator
text: Countless mirrors show false paths and twisted reflections. Find the one true way through the labyrinth.

speaker: narrator
text: The pendant's light falls on the glass. Here every reflection walks with you; there is nothing yet to choose between.

speaker: narrator
text: You retrace your steps out of the glass.

speaker: narrator
text: The Knight of Despair

speaker: narrator
text: A knight in a grey cloak stands before the stair to the Tower of Shadows and does not move. Learn the truth of him, and find a way past.

speaker: narrator
text: You stand still and listen. Beneath the battle cries and laments, one voice repeats the same words over and over, patient as a heartbeat:

speaker: an echo
text: 'Left, then left, then the way your shadow does not go.'

speaker: narrator
text: You lift a smooth grey stone from a niche beneath the banners. It is warm, and when you hold it to your ear you hear the hall's echoes still speaking inside it.

speaker: narrator
text: You turn left, and the glass lets you through.

speaker: narrator
text: You turn left again, and the glass lets you through.

speaker: narrator
text: The pendant's blue light falls on the glass. In the north corridor your reflection turns and walks with you. In the east corridor the glass stays empty.

speaker: narrator
text: You step into the empty corridor. Behind you the false mirrors go dark, one by one, until a single corridor remains. At its end stands a plain mirror that shows you exactly as you are.

speaker: narrator
text: You have learned Truth Sight.

speaker: narrator
text: Guided by the servants' pendant and the hall's echoes, Elior walks the one true path through the mirrors, and learns to see through illusion.

speaker: narrator
text: Your sight sharpens, and the gloom peels away from the knight. His grey cloak is a traveller's, hooded and road-worn, and its clasp bears a twisted rune you know: the rune on the token that fouled Willowbrook's well, and the seal on the secret documents that cleared Sir Cedric's name. This is the cloaked stranger the villagers whispered about. Behind the visor, the knight is weeping.

speaker: narrator
text: Your sight sharpens, and the grime slides from the banners. Beneath it is the sigil of the gate company of King Alden's guard, and the same sigil shows through the tarnish on the knight's breastplate. He served the king before he ever served Malakar.

speaker: narrator
text: Your sight sharpens, and the stone's murmur parts. Under the hall's voices, the one that keeps saying redemption is weeping, and between the words it says one more, very quietly.

speaker: knight of despair
text: Sorry.

speaker: narrator
text: It is the knight's voice.

speaker: narrator
text: You open your mouth, and the knight's despair rolls over you like cold water. The word dies in your throat. Nothing stands between you and his sorrow, and the chain is gone with the captain. But you are not as alone as the knight would have you believe.

speaker: narrator
text: A small blue crystal on a fine chain, from the freed servants. When you hold it, it feels as if someone is standing just behind you, ready to point the way.

speaker: narrator
text: The Freed Servants bow. One of them, an old woman with flour still in the creases of her hands, looks up.

speaker: freed servants
text: I was the king's cook. I do not know how long ago.

speaker: narrator
text: The Captain of the Guard lifts his head and meets your eyes.

speaker: captain of the guard
text: I remember now. King Alden used to walk the walls at night and talk to whoever was on them. That is how they got him. Cedric stood his post. They came in by the king's postern, and it had been left unguarded. If you see Sir Cedric again, tell him I am sorry I ever doubted him.

speaker: captain of the guard
text: They tell me the gates are open. I would walk out of them tonight, if my hand remembered the sword. Every shadow between here and home knows my face.

speaker: narrator
text: The freed servants sit by the fountains in their kitchen aprons and stable coats, rubbing their ankles where the chains were.

speaker: narrator
text: A captain of the royal guard, his tabard black with soot. He sits among the servants, opening and closing his sword hand as if it belonged to someone else.

speaker: narrator
text: The pendant glows faintly. Whoever is behind you has nothing to say here.

speaker: narrator
text: Mirror Labyrinth

speaker: narrator
text: Corridors of mirror run away from you in every direction, and in each of them a different Elior looks back. You stand at the mouth of the maze, facing north.

speaker: narrator
text: Each mirror shows a different Elior — older, younger, crowned, broken — with a different corridor stretching away behind him. Every path looks real. Most of them are lies.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Mirror Labyrinth, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The Maze of Mirrors: Countless mirrors show false paths and twisted reflections. Find the one true way through the labyrinth.

speaker: narrator
text: Hall of Echoes

speaker: narrator
text: A long hall of old banners, so high the ceiling is lost. Everything that was ever said here is still being said, very quietly: orders, jokes, names, someone counting. Tattered banners hang high along the walls, grimed past reading. At the far end, before the stair, a knight in tarnished armour stands without moving, the way a man stands at a grave. Sir Cedric stands by the south door, the way out at his back, his eyes on the knight.

speaker: narrator
text: A smooth grey stone that hums with the voices of the Hall of Echoes. Held close, it repeats what the echoes know.

speaker: narrator
text: Tattered banners hang high along the walls, too grimed with age to read. Something is stitched beneath the dirt.

speaker: narrator
text: You hold the loyalty token close to your heart. For a moment you are not alone in the hall: Mira at the gate, the light on the gatepost, the servants you freed. The knight's despair breaks around you and does not reach you.

speaker: narrator
text: You hold the chain up between you and the knight. The crystals catch what little light there is and keep it. His sorrow is still there, but it no longer reaches you.

speaker: narrator
text: The light steadies in the old hall, as if it has been here before.

speaker: knight of despair
text: There is nothing you can say to me that I have not already told myself. Go. Return when you have the truth.

speaker: sir cedric
text: That voice. I have heard it before, Elior, on the king's walls. I would swear to it. I cannot see the face that goes with it.

speaker: narrator
text: A knight in tarnished armour, a shredded grey cloak hanging from his shoulders. He stands with his back to the door you came in by. His visor is down, and he does not move. When he speaks, his voice is hollow.

speaker: knight of despair
text: Return when you have the truth.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric, by the south door, his eyes on the knight.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Hall of Echoes, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The Knight of Despair: A knight in a grey cloak stands before the stair to the Tower of Shadows and does not move. Learn the truth of him, and find a way past.

speaker: narrator
text: You hold the echo stone to your ear. The hall's voices murmur inside it, waiting for somewhere that needs them. Under the rest, one voice says a single word over and over, the way a man says a word he has stopped believing in: redemption.

speaker: narrator
text: You step toward a corridor of light and walk straight into cold glass. Somewhere behind you, a reflection laughs. You are back at the entrance.

speaker: narrator
text: You listen for a voice to follow, but in here the glass answers only with your own. You lose the way, and find yourself back at the entrance.

speaker: narrator
text: The stone is warm, and the hall's echoes still speak inside it.

speaker: narrator
text: You hold the echo stone to your ear. One voice repeats, patient as a heartbeat:

speaker: an echo
text: Left, then left, then the way your shadow does not go.

speaker: narrator
text: Your reflection still walks the north corridor. The east corridor stays empty.

speaker: true self
text: You tell everyone you came for the king. Tell me the truth: why did you really come?

speaker: narrator
text: You tell it the truth: that you did not come only for the king. You came because you want Malakar to pay for what he took from you, and you are afraid of what that wanting makes you. The reflection nods, slowly. For a moment it wears your father's face. Then it is only you again, standing a little straighter.

speaker: true self
text: Remember what you told me, when you stand before him.

speaker: narrator
text: The true path is already clear. The false mirrors stay dark.

speaker: narrator
text: Your own reflection, in the plain mirror at the labyrinth's heart. It does not copy you. It waits, watching, as if it already knows what you will say.

speaker: narrator
text: The word means nothing to a man you cannot truly see. He does not even turn his head.

speaker: narrator
text: The Knight of Despair stands before the stair to the tower. He does not lift his sword. He simply does not move, and there is no way past him.

speaker: narrator
text: The word catches in your throat. You have seen something of him, but you do not yet know what he has done. There is more in this hall to see through.

speaker: knight of despair
text: So you see something of me. That is not the same as knowing me. Look around you, if you must know.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Grey cloak, twisted rune. I know him now. Do what you came to do. I will hear what he has to say.

speaker: narrator
text: The grey cloak, the twisted rune at its clasp, the tears behind the visor. The cloaked stranger from Willowbrook stands before you, and he knows you have seen him.

speaker: narrator
text: You open your mouth, and the knight's despair rolls over you like cold water. The word dies in your throat. You could not say it with nothing between you and his sorrow.

speaker: knight of despair
text: So you see me. Then you know what I am, and what I have done. There is no redemption for a man like me. Do not waste the word.

speaker: narrator
text: The chain is already lit. His sorrow does not reach you.

speaker: narrator
text: The knight's despair breaks against the chain's light like a wave on stone. Slowly he turns round to face you, and lifts his visor. The face beneath is grey and tired, and very human.

speaker: sir cedric
text: You.

speaker: knight of despair
text: Me.

speaker: knight of despair
text: I was the stranger in Willowbrook. Malakar sent me for an amulet, and for the child of the house that kept it. It was my token that fouled your well.

speaker: knight of despair
text: I stood on that gate once, in the king's colours. The night King Alden was taken, I paid the watch to look away. The captain of the watch was a good man. I made sure he was asleep. And I put my seal to the lie that shamed Sir Cedric.

speaker: knight of despair
text: And when I saw what my master was doing to the king, I stopped believing he could be saved. That is all despair is. Then you walked in and said the word I had stopped saying.

speaker: knight of despair
text: Sir Cedric. I am sorry. I have no right to ask anything of you, so I will not.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric does not move from the door.

speaker: sir cedric
text: I heard you. That will have to be enough, for now.

speaker: narrator
text: With his despair gone from the hall, you see what it was hiding: pale soldiers among the banners, still fighting.

speaker: narrator
text: He unpins a tarnished badge from his breast and presses it into your hand.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive the knight's redemption.

speaker: narrator
text: The echo stone grows warm. Inside it the knight's voice has stopped repeating its one word; it speaks plainly now, and what it says is true.

speaker: narrator
text: You have learned Redemption's Light. Light that reminds a fallen soul of who it was.

speaker: narrator
text: The Knight of Despair was the stranger from Willowbrook. He fouled the well, framed Sir Cedric and let the king be taken, and he confessed it to Sir Cedric's face.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior sees the knight as he truly is and offers him redemption instead of a blade. The man who framed Sir Cedric confesses, and the stair to the Tower of Shadows lies open.

speaker: narrator
text: Soft light spills from your hands across the hall. One by one the ghostly warriors lower their blades. One puts a hand on another's shoulder. Then they fade, at peace.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric watches the last of them go. Then he crosses the hall and offers the knight his hand.

speaker: sir cedric
text: If they can be let go, so can this. I forgive you. Get up.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Go on up. I will wait here with him. Someone should.

speaker: narrator
text: The echo stone hums more strongly now. Among the hall's voices one speaks clearly and without fear: the knight's, telling the truth.

speaker: narrator
text: A tarnished knight's badge, warm to the touch. He pressed it into your hand: proof that even one of Malakar's own can turn back.

speaker: narrator
text: You hold the stone to your ear. The voices inside it are clearer now, waiting for a place where memories sleep.

speaker: redeemed knight
text: I will wait here. If you come back down those stairs, I will know there is still hope.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Go on up. I will keep an eye on him.

speaker: narrator
text: The warriors do not hear you. They are still fighting.

speaker: narrator
text: He kneels by the stair, his helm beside him. Without the visor he looks like any tired soldier far from home.

speaker: narrator
text: Pale shapes of soldiers drift among the banners, fighting a battle that ended long ago. Their blades pass through one another without a sound.

speaker: narrator
text: The Final Stand: The Knight of Despair was the stranger from Willowbrook. He fouled the well, framed Sir Cedric and let the king be taken, and he confessed it to Sir Cedric's face.

speaker: narrator
text: You set your foot on the stair, and the whispers close in: your friends have left you, no one is coming, you were always alone. You stumble back down.

speaker: narrator
text: Tower of Shadows

speaker: narrator
text: A stair winds up inside the black stone, narrow and dark. The walls are cold, and there are no windows. The shadows on the stair move a moment after you do. With every step, something quiet at your ear tells you why you should not have come.

speaker: narrator
text: You hold the token up, and it grows warm. Under the whispers, very faint, you think you hear your name, in Mira's voice, and what she said at the gate: say our names.

speaker: narrator
text: They do not answer you. They only say it again, closer: your friends have left you. No one is coming. Name one who stayed. You cannot.

speaker: narrator
text: Voices without mouths, thick on the stair, saying the same thing again and again.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Tower of Shadows, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The token warms against your palm, and the whispers falter.

speaker: mira
text: I'm at the gate, Elior. I said I'd hold it, and I'm holding it.

speaker: narrator
text: The token warms again. The whispers draw back from the stair.

speaker: sir cedric
text: I am in the hall behind you, Elior. I have not left. Go on up.

speaker: narrator
text: The token warms against your palm. A small light flickers at the edge of your eye, and in your pack the crystalline pendant she gave you, Nyx's Token, is warm too.

speaker: nyx
text: Left? I'm right here. I never was anywhere else.

speaker: narrator
text: The whispers have nothing left to say. They thin like smoke, and the stair above lies open.

speaker: narrator
text: The token is quiet and warm. The whispers are gone.

speaker: narrator
text: The Sorceress of Lies

speaker: narrator
text: At the top of the tower the Sorceress of Lies holds court, and the mask on her staff is the mark from Elena's wrist. Listen past her lies, to what is under them.

speaker: narrator
text: She laughs, and the chamber laughs with her. Whatever you came to give her is lost among the whispers.

speaker: narrator
text: The north arch is a wall of whispering crystal. It will not open while the Sorceress holds the chamber.

speaker: narrator
text: Chamber of Whispers

speaker: narrator
text: A round room at the top of the tower, and the only beautiful room in the fortress. That is what is wrong with it. Crystals grow from the walls, each humming something kind and untrue, and the floor gives a little under your feet, like ice that might hold. At the chamber's heart the Sorceress of Lies waits, her staff crowned with a small silver mask. Your breath catches: it is the mask from Elena's wrist.

speaker: narrator
text: The mask is smooth and smiling, with no eyes behind it. It is the very mark that sat on Elena's wrist in Greendale. The woman who carries this staff cursed her.

speaker: narrator
text: You lean close to a crystal. The whispers speak of what you want most and fear most, and the longer you listen the more they sound alike.

speaker: narrator
text: The token is still warm against your heart. Her whispers cannot reach you.

speaker: narrator
text: The Sorceress stares at the knight's badge, and for the first time her smile slips. Beneath the whispers you hear something else: a voice, very small, that is not lying.

speaker: narrator
text: You have learned Heart's Truth. Hear the true heart beneath a lie.

speaker: sorceress of lies
text: Little Elior. Your parents sold you to save themselves, did you know? For a sack of grain, in a hungry winter. Turn back.

speaker: narrator
text: She is beautiful in the way the chamber is beautiful: a little too perfect, a little wrong. Her smile never reaches her eyes.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Chamber of Whispers, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The Sorceress of Lies: At the top of the tower the Sorceress of Lies holds court, and the mask on her staff is the mark from Elena's wrist. Listen past her lies, to what is under them.

speaker: narrator
text: You cannot answer a pain you cannot hear. Beneath the whispers her heart is saying something, too quietly for ears alone.

speaker: narrator
text: She has seen the badge. She cannot stop looking at it.

speaker: sorceress of lies
text: He turned? Then he is a fool. Everyone lies, little Elior. No one has ever understood a word I said. Why would you be the first?

speaker: narrator
text: The whispers fall away. Beneath them the Sorceress is alone, as she has always been: no one has ever spoken to her without a lie, and she has never answered with anything else.

speaker: narrator
text: And under the loneliness, older and smaller: a girl in a hungry winter, and the parents who sold her for a sack of grain. It is the only story about parents she has ever known.

speaker: narrator
text: You have heard some of her, but not all. There is more in this chamber that is hers to listen to.

speaker: narrator
text: You listen, and beneath the mask's smile there is something small and lonely. It was made to be looked at, and no one ever looked at it. Only away.

speaker: narrator
text: You listen to the crystals, and the whispers are not many voices. They are one: hers, repeating every lie she has ever told so that she never has to hear the silence.

speaker: elior
text: I understand. You have been alone in here a long time.

speaker: narrator
text: The Sorceress goes very still. One by one the crystals stop whispering, until the chamber is silent for the first time in years.

speaker: sorceress of lies
text: Elena. The girl at the inn. Malakar wanted every healer in the kingdom at her bedside and none at the king's. So I cursed her, and set my mask on her wrist so they would know whose work it was, and fear it. And I watched the inn door, to see who would come for a mark like that. The healer from Willowbrook never did. I should have known then what that meant.

speaker: sorceress of lies
text: I told the king's physicians he was only tired. I have told so many lies that I forgot what my own voice sounds like. And I told you your parents sold you. Mine did. I wanted it to be true of everyone, so that it would not only be true of me.

speaker: sorceress of lies
text: No one has ever spoken to me without a lie. Not Malakar, not his servants, not the ones I cursed. You are the first. I did not know it would hurt.

speaker: narrator
text: She lifts the silver mask from her staff and puts it in your hands.

speaker: narrator
text: You receive the sorceress's truth.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior listens past the Sorceress's lies and answers the loneliness beneath them. She confesses the curse on Elena, and the arch to the north opens.

speaker: narrator
text: You turn the mask over in your hands. Somewhere ahead is someone who needs to see that a liar can choose the truth.

speaker: narrator
text: Her staff lies across her knees, bare where the mask once sat.

speaker: narrator
text: The crystals are silent now.

speaker: narrator
text: The silver mask from her staff, smooth and smiling, with no eyes behind it. In your hands it is only metal: a lie she no longer needs, given as proof that even a liar can choose the truth.

speaker: unmasked sorceress
text: Go on, through the arch. What waits there has been waiting for you longer than I have. And Elior — tell Elena I am sorry. It is the first true thing I have asked anyone to carry.

speaker: narrator
text: Without the chamber's glamour she looks tired and ordinary, a woman who has not slept in years. She keeps her eyes on the arch.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shadow of the Past

speaker: narrator
text: Among the broken memories a shadow reaches for scenes it cannot hold. Mend what it has lost, and learn whose voice it is.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shadow does not see you. The memories around it are too broken.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shadow cannot see the mask through the broken memories.

speaker: narrator
text: A round door of pale stone, carved with the same runes as your amulet around the sigil of the Wardens of the Dawn, and beneath it, worn almost away, a tree under two moons: the crest on your mother's locket. It has no handle and no keyhole.

speaker: narrator
text: The door's runes stay dark under the amulet. The Shadow is still watching you.

speaker: narrator
text: The sealed door will not move. Its runes are dark.

speaker: narrator
text: Memory Vault

speaker: narrator
text: Glass orbs hang in the air at every height, each one cracked, each one holding a scene that breaks apart before it settles. Among them stands a shadow in the shape of a man. In the east wall is a round door of pale stone.

speaker: narrator
text: The orbs are cracked and clouded. In one you glimpse three young people laughing over a workbench; in another, a cradle by a fire. Each scene breaks apart before you can hold it. From the cracked one by the cradle a voice sings, low:

speaker: narrator
text: Hush, little seed—

speaker: narrator
text: It breaks off.

speaker: narrator
text: You raise the echo stone. The voices inside it pour out into the vault, and the orbs drink them in. One by one the cracks close and the scenes grow still and clear. The shadow turns towards you, and for the first time it has a face.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Elior. You came.

speaker: narrator
text: You know the voice before you know the face. It is the voice from your dream, the one that called your name on the stormy night in Willowbrook, and in Nyx's vision, and in the Dragon's hall.

speaker: narrator
text: The shadow's lips move, but the vault swallows the sound.

speaker: narrator
text: It is the shape of a man, thin as smoke. It reaches for the orbs, and they slip through its fingers.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Memory Vault, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shadow of the Past: Among the broken memories a shadow reaches for scenes it cannot hold. Mend what it has lost, and learn whose voice it is.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shadow of the Past shakes its head.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Patience is for those who still have hope. I have none left.

speaker: narrator
text: Whole now. In one, three young Wardens laugh over a workbench; in another, a cradle sits by a fire. The clearest scenes all lie beyond the door to the east.

speaker: narrator
text: A family heirloom whose runes glint like dew at dawn. In its depths Aren and Lysa stand hand in hand. The third figure keeps his back turned. He is young; you can see it in the set of his shoulders.

speaker: narrator
text: The orbs are whole. The stone lies quiet in your hand.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shadow turns the silver mask over in hands that are almost solid now, and gives it back.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: She lied for him for years, and still she chose the truth. Then perhaps he can too. But not by force, Elior. Never by force.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: I was Malakar, once. Not the one in the throne room. The part of him that remembered why he began. When he tore the wound, he left me behind. I have called to you since you were small.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: The same words, every time. You caught pieces. Hear them whole. Be patient where I was not. Close what I opened, and let them rest.

speaker: narrator
text: A man made of shadow, almost solid now. His face is kind and very tired. You have never seen it before, and you know it all the same.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shadow has seen the mask. It is enough.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: The Phoenix asked me once what wisdom is when time is short. I gave it the right answer. Then the fever came, and I did not keep it.

speaker: narrator
text: You sit down among the orbs and wait, and say nothing at all. The Shadow watches you do it for a long time.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Patience. The one thing I never had. Then I will wait, a little longer. Take the amulet east, Elior. It will open for you.

speaker: elior
text: Patience. You could not wait for them. You can wait a little longer, for me.

speaker: narrator
text: The voice from your dreams is what is left of Malakar's better self. It said its words whole at last: Be patient where I was not. Close what I opened, and let them rest.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior learns that the voice from his dreams is what remains of Malakar's better self. The sealed door to the east now answers to the amulet.

speaker: narrator
text: The door is sealed. Its runes glow faintly, waiting for the amulet.

speaker: narrator
text: A round door of pale stone, carved with the same runes as your amulet around the sigil of the Wardens of the Dawn, and beneath it, worn almost away, a tree under two moons: the crest on your mother's locket. The runes glow faintly now, as if they are waiting.

speaker: narrator
text: The runes on the door wake to the runes on the amulet, and the stone rolls aside without a sound.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Go east, Elior. I have seen those memories every day for years. You never have.

speaker: narrator
text: The Final Stand: The voice from your dreams is what is left of Malakar's better self. It said its words whole at last: Be patient where I was not. Close what I opened, and let them rest.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shadow has its answer. It nods towards the door to the east.

speaker: narrator
text: The Parent's Legacy

speaker: narrator
text: Behind the sealed door, Aren and Lysa's last memories wait. Look into them, and learn the whole truth before the throne room.

speaker: narrator
text: The door to the north is shut. The lanterns are still waiting for you.

speaker: narrator
text: Parents' Vault

speaker: narrator
text: A small, quiet room. Nothing here is threatening. Memories hang in the air like lanterns, warm and still, and every one of them has your parents in it. It is the saddest and warmest room in the fortress.

speaker: narrator
text: Three young Wardens bent over one workbench: your father, your mother, and a dark-haired man laughing at something Lysa said. Between them lie a crystal, a feather and a scale.

speaker: narrator
text: The year before you were born. The Wasting: a fever sweeps the land, and Aren and Lysa fall ill with it. Nothing the Wardens know can heal them. Malakar sits by their beds, reading, searching, unable to wait.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar alone in a room full of clocks, tearing the air open to pull back the days before the fever. Aren and Lysa wake, well again. But the wound he opened does not close, and it begins to feed.

speaker: narrator
text: It is still pulling. Every clock in the room runs backwards, wanting more of the days back, and the wound would take all of them if nothing held it shut.

speaker: narrator
text: Your parents before the wound, hands joined, pouring themselves into a seal across it until they are only light, bound to the amulet and to the crown of King Alden, so that you would be hidden and the wound held shut.

speaker: lysa
text: Hold it shut, Aren. Hide him. That is enough.

speaker: narrator
text: The ward is Aren and Lysa, and it lives in you. Their gift is the magic you have: every spell that ever answered your hands came through them, all but one, which you read from a stone in a glade.

speaker: narrator
text: Last, and smallest: Malakar by a cottage fire in Willowbrook, rocking a baby in his arms and singing, low:

speaker: malakar
text: Hush, little seed, the frost is going. Hush, the field will wake.

speaker: narrator
text: The baby is you.

speaker: narrator
text: The lanterns dim, one by one, until only the amulet glows in your hand.

speaker: narrator
text: Your parents sold you to save themselves. It was the opposite. They gave themselves away to save you. You are sure now.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Parents' Vault, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The Parent's Legacy: Behind the sealed door, Aren and Lysa's last memories wait. Look into them, and learn the whole truth before the throne room.

speaker: narrator
text: In the vault you saw it all. Malakar tore at time to save your parents from the Wasting. They poured themselves into the ward that holds his wound shut, and the ward lives in you. Malakar waits past the north door.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior sees the whole truth: his parents' friendship with Malakar, the wound, and the ward they became. The way north to the Throne Chamber opens.

speaker: narrator
text: The lanterns are dim now. You do not need to look again; you will not forget.

speaker: narrator
text: The Final Stand: In the vault you saw it all. Malakar tore at time to save your parents from the Wasting. They poured themselves into the ward that holds his wound shut, and the ward lives in you. Malakar waits past the north door.

speaker: narrator
text: Throne Chamber

speaker: narrator
text: A vast chamber under a broken dome. A throne of black stone, twisted like a root, stands at its head. Above a ritual circle King Alden hangs in a prison of crystal, and from his crown a thin thread of light bleeds into a rift in the air: the wound in time. Malakar stands beside it, grey and failing. The wound is killing him too.

speaker: narrator
text: The crystal is clouded and cold. Inside it King Alden sleeps without breathing, his crown dark. A thread of light runs from his crown into the wound.

speaker: narrator
text: A tear in the air, no wider than a door, its edges flickering with days that never happened. It drinks the light from the king, and from Malakar too.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar lunges for the amulet. The moment his fingers close on it, it burns white, and he snatches his hand back.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Not like this.

speaker: narrator
text: The voice is gone as soon as it came. Malakar holds his hand against his chest and will not look at you.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar's hand comes up for the elixir, and stops a finger's width from the glass.

speaker: malakar
text: You would waste it on me? You have not even heard what I am offering.

speaker: malakar
text: Aren's son. You have their eyes, both of them. You have seen the vault, so you know what I did, and you know it worked. They woke, Elior. For a little while, they woke.

speaker: malakar
text: The wound runs backwards. Open it all the way and it pulls the days back to before the fever, and they wake at the workbench as they were. I am not lying to you. I have done the sums.

speaker: malakar
text: Only the ward holds it shut: half in your amulet, half in Alden's crown. Since my man brought him here I have been bleeding the king to loosen his half. Give me yours and the bleeding stops today.

speaker: malakar
text: And the price is the rest of it. The king. Every year the kingdom has had since. And you. You were born after the tear, Elior. When the days go back, you go with them. I am sorry. The sums are still right.

speaker: narrator
text: King Alden sleeps in the crystal and does not hear you.

speaker: narrator
text: A tall man in a grey robe that was once a Warden's blue. His hair is white, though he cannot be much older than your father would have been. He leans on the throne as if it is the only thing holding him up. He is looking at the wound, not at you.

speaker: narrator
text: The king of Eldoria, grey and thin, as if each week in here had been a year. His crown is dark.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Throne Chamber, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar's hand closes on the amulet, and for a moment neither of you lets go. Then you do.

speaker: narrator
text: He lifts it toward the thread of light that bleeds from the king's crown. The wound in the air yawns wide, and the chamber goes grey, and then gold.

speaker: narrator
text: A workshop in the late sun. Aren bends over the workbench; Lysa laughs at something he has said. They are young. They do not look up.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Not like this. Not by force.

speaker: narrator
text: The amulet will not break. The light runs backwards through the chamber and Malakar is thrown against the throne. You are standing where you stood, and the amulet is warm in your hand.

speaker: malakar
text: You saw. Then you know I was not lying.

speaker: elior
text: Power follows purpose; purpose follows truth.

speaker: narrator
text: The words from the stone in Willowbrook, from Nyx, from the Dragon's hall. They are yours now.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar turns from the wound. For the first time since you came in, he is looking at you.

speaker: malakar
text: We carved those words together, your father and I. I had forgotten them.

speaker: narrator
text: The amulet opens in your hand like a flower, and the light of the ward pours out over the chamber. Malakar staggers. When he speaks again, it is not his voice.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Elior. I tore the world to keep them, and I lost them anyway. Be patient where I was not. Close what I opened, and let them rest.

speaker: narrator
text: The lifelight elixir is warm in your hand. It can be used only once. It could break the crystal and free the king, or it could be offered to Malakar, to heal the wound that is killing him.

speaker: narrator
text: You kneel and hold the elixir to Malakar's lips. He drinks. The grey goes out of his face, and for a moment he is the young man at the workbench again.

speaker: malakar
text: Hush, little seed,

speaker: narrator
text: he sings under his breath, and does not seem to know he does. The wound flickers, and waits.

speaker: narrator
text: The lifelight elixir is gone.

speaker: elior
text: I forgive you.

speaker: narrator
text: The words are harder than any spell, and then they are easy.

speaker: narrator
text: You have learned forgiveness.

speaker: malakar
text: You would forgive me. They would have too.

speaker: narrator
text: Forgiveness settles on the wound, and its edges stop flickering. The days that never happened fall quiet one by one, and the tear draws closed like a healed cut. Above the circle the crystal clouds, cracks and falls away, and King Alden breathes again.

speaker: malakar
text: Thank you, Elior. I will stay here, by what I broke, and remember them properly this time.

speaker: narrator
text: Where the wound was, the light of the amulet gathers into two shapes you have only ever seen in pictures and memories: a man with your eyes, and a woman with Grandmother's smile. Your parents.

speaker: aren
text: Elior. Look at you. Taller than me, I think.

speaker: lysa
text: We watched over you all this time, from inside the light. We could not hold you, but we could hold the door shut.

speaker: lysa
text: We saw you at the workbench with us, for a moment. You let it go. That was the bravest thing you did today.

speaker: lysa
text: You gave him back to us, our friend. We never dared hope for that.

speaker: aren
text: The ward is finished, and so are we. Tell your grandmother we are proud of her. Tell her we are resting.

speaker: lysa
text: Go home, love. The field is waiting.

speaker: narrator
text: The light thins. They smile, and they are gone. The amulet in your hand is dark now, and still warm. Your parents are at rest.

speaker: narrator
text: Behind the throne an arch you had not noticed stands open. Beyond it, far off, the road runs home.

speaker: narrator
text: Main quest complete

speaker: narrator
text: The wound is closed and the king is free. Your parents are at rest.

speaker: narrator
text: You walk out of the fortress and do not look back. The road home is long, and somehow shorter than it was. Days later the hedges of Willowbrook close around you, and then you are standing at the edge of your own field.

speaker: narrator
text: Nobody has touched it since you left.

speaker: narrator
text: At the gate Grandmother is humming to herself: a slow tune that climbs three notes and settles home again. You are humming it with her before you know it. She stops.

speaker: narrator
text: You kneel at the edge of the field. Your hands remember the spell you read from a stone in the glade, the one that was always yours.

speaker: narrator
text: You have learned grow.

speaker: narrator
text: You press your hands into the dry earth and say the smallest spell you know. Green runs out from your fingers along the rows. Leaves unfurl, the earth darkens, and the whole field breathes out at once.

speaker: narrator
text: Across the village, the chapel bell rings once, with no hand on the rope.

speaker: grandmother
text: That is the third time. The first was for her, the night she went. The second was for you, the morning you left. I do not know who this one is for.

speaker: narrator
text: You do.

speaker: narrator
text: In the hedge the little light brightens. For the last time you hear Nyx, very small:

speaker: nyx
text: Power follows purpose; purpose follows truth.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandmother opens the gate.

speaker: grandmother
text: Welcome home, Elior.

speaker: narrator
text: You pour the elixir over the crystal. It cracks like ice in spring, and King Alden falls free, gasping, alive. But the wound still stands open, and Malakar still stands beside it.

speaker: elior
text: You tore the world, Malakar. You drained the king. You sent a man to hunt a child in Willowbrook, and you had Sir Cedric framed for taking the king. I will not pretend you didn't.

speaker: malakar
text: No. You won't. Your mother never could either.

speaker: narrator
text: The open amulet grows heavy in your hand, ready.

speaker: narrator
text: You press the open amulet to the wound. Threads of gold rise from King Alden's crown and weave into the ward's light. The tear closes, and Malakar goes with it, drawn into the seal. He does not fight.

speaker: malakar
text: I am sorry. Tell them— no. They know.

speaker: narrator
text: The last of him to go is his voice, low:

speaker: malakar
text: …the field will wake.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the seal is shut.

speaker: king alden
text: Then it falls to me to set right what he broke. Rest now. You have done enough.

speaker: aren
text: You named what he did, and you did not hate him for it. That is the hardest kind of fair.

speaker: king alden
text: The kingdom will remember what you did here, farmer. I will see that it does.

speaker: elior
text: Take my magic. All of it. Close the wound with that.

speaker: malakar
text: No. Your parents gave themselves to hold that wound shut. It does not get to have you too.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar half rises, reaching for the amulet, and stops his own hand.

speaker: malakar
text: Then keep something. One thing. Anything. Do not let me take it all.

speaker: narrator
text: You press the open amulet to the wound and let go. The light, the blessing, the truth sight, every spell you carried runs out of your hands into the tear, and the tear drinks it and closes. When it is done, one small spell is still in you: grow, the one you read from a stone in a glade.

speaker: narrator
text: Your magic is gone. Only grow remains.

speaker: king alden
text: He will answer to me, and he will live to do it. Thank you, farmer.

speaker: lysa
text: You gave our gift back to close what he opened, and kept the one thing that was yours.

speaker: king alden
text: You have earned your field, farmer. No one will take it from you.

speaker: narrator
text: You kneel at the edge of the field. The one spell you kept stirs in your hands, small and certain.

speaker: malakar
text: You would waste it on me? Keep it for them, then. Give me the amulet, Elior, and your mother wakes before that glass is empty.

speaker: malakar
text: They would wake, Elior. Your mother would laugh at something your father said. Is one boy and one tired king too much to pay for that? Give me the amulet.

speaker: narrator
text: A family heirloom whose runes glint like dew at dawn. In its depths Aren and Lysa stand hand in hand. The third figure keeps his back turned, but his head is up, as if someone has said his name.

speaker: narrator
text: Not yet. The amulet at your chest is stirring.

speaker: malakar
text: Then show me what they left you.

speaker: narrator
text: A tall man in a grey robe that was once a Warden's blue. His hair is white, though he cannot be much older than your father would have been. He leans on the throne as if it is the only thing holding him up, and he does not look away from you.

speaker: king alden
text: You came for me. Whoever you are, you came.

speaker: king alden
text: You named every crime and did not add one. Few men in my court could do that.

speaker: aren
text: We watched you give, again and again, and never ask for anything back. Today was only the last time.

speaker: narrator
text: Not yet. The elixir is still in your hand.

speaker: narrator
text: Not yet. The elixir is still in your hand. After that, you could forgive him. You could name his crimes and seal him away, in justice. Or you could give up your magic to close the wound, in sacrifice.

speaker: narrator
text: The amulet is already open, its light filling the chamber.

speaker: narrator
text: The elixir is for the king's prison, or for Malakar's wound.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar does not answer. He is staring at the open amulet.

speaker: malakar
text: And not for the first time, I think. You have shown mercy before, where none was owed. I can see it on you.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar has drunk the elixir. That road is closed now.

speaker: malakar
text: It does not hurt. For the first time in years, it does not hurt.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar looks up at you like a man waiting to be forgiven.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar is already forgiven. It is the wound that needs it.

speaker: narrator
text: The crystal lies in shards around the ritual circle.

speaker: narrator
text: The air where the wound was is still and empty.

speaker: narrator
text: A family heirloom whose runes glint like dew at dawn. In its depths Aren and Lysa stand hand in hand. The third figure has turned around. The three of them stand together at a workbench, heads bent over something you cannot quite see.

speaker: narrator
text: The amulet is dark now, and still warm.

speaker: malakar
text: Go home, Elior. Tell Mira I am sorry, and that I remember her.

speaker: king alden
text: You saved my kingdom, and somehow him as well. I would not have known how.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar sits by the shards, himself again.

speaker: narrator
text: The king of Eldoria, alive, his crown bright again.

speaker: narrator
text: Willowbrook Field

speaker: narrator
text: The field behind your home: rows of withered crops under a pale sky, the earth cracked and grey. Grandmother waits at the gate. Mira stands beside her, and Sir Cedric leans on the fence. In the hedge a small light flickers: Nyx, keeping close. The air is quiet.

speaker: grandmother
text: Your mother's. I didn't think you'd remember.

speaker: grandmother
text: You saw them. I can see it in your face.

speaker: elior
text: You knew.

speaker: narrator
text: It is not a question.

speaker: grandmother
text: I knew. She made me promise, the night she went. I have not slept a whole night since.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her what they said: that they are proud of her, that they are resting.

speaker: grandmother
text: Resting. Good. Then so can we. Go on, dear. The field first. The bread will keep.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her Malakar is himself again, and alive.

speaker: mira
text: Himself. Then I will go and see him, one day. Not yet.

speaker: sir cedric
text: The knight in grey said his piece to my face. I have not forgiven him. Not yet.

speaker: narrator
text: He looks out over the field for a while.

speaker: sir cedric
text: I have walked a long way beside you. This is a good place to stop.

speaker: narrator
text: The little light brushes your cheek, warm, and settles back into the hedge.

speaker: narrator
text: Your grandmother at the gate, flour still on her apron. For once her hands are still.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira, standing beside Grandmother at the gate.

speaker: narrator
text: Sir Cedric, leaning on the fence as if it were a wall.

speaker: narrator
text: A small light in the hedge. The leaves are greener where it has settled.

speaker: narrator
text: You search around the Willowbrook Field, but find nothing of interest beyond what you can already see.

speaker: narrator
text: The light comes down to the pendant, and the two of them are gone into the hedge together; a moment later the light is back, a little steadier, and your hand is empty.

speaker: narrator
text: The light brushes the servant's pendant once and leaves it in your hand. It is yours.

speaker: narrator
text: The light brushes the ancient amulet once and leaves it in your hand. It is yours.

speaker: narrator
text: Nyx glows briefly with golden light.

speaker: narrator
text: Grow is for the field, not for people.

speaker: narrator
text: Act IV complete. The Final Confrontation.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar is himself again. And Elior is home.
